title: LoopROS: A Dual Recursive Self-Improvement Loops of Robotic Operating System Based on Functional Constraints and Trajectory Tuning
content: Recent advances in foundation models have enabled robotic agents to reason, plan, and adapt their actions through physical interaction. Yet successful execution does not necessarily translate into lasting improvement across tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising paradigm for robotic agents to continuously refine their capabilities through experience, but requires preserving functional knowledge, adapting execution to changing physical conditions, and retaining reusable corrections. We introduce LoopROS, a dual-loop robotic agent framework that couples functionally constrained execution with experience-driven improvement. Within each episode, functional constraint-guided in-context learning identifies essential task relations from demonstrations and context, while visual feedback-guided segmentwise trajectory tuning adapts reference motions through observation-grounded corrections and verification. Across episodes, execution feedback informs revisions to persistent skills, parameters, and executable tools, enabling subsequent executions to reuse corrections under relevant conditions. The LoopROS achieves an 82.0% success rate and a mean score of 88.90, ranking No. 1 in RoboDojo, among the compared methods. We further complete 30 successful trials in three real robot manipulation tasks, elucidating its great potential as a backbone robotic RSI.
